27:1.sourceText: Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης συμβούλιον ἔλαβον πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὥστε θανατῶσαι αὐτόν·
27:1.targetText: When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus to put Him to death.

groups.note: The genitive absolute Πρωΐας γενομένης is rendered as a When-clause.
συμβούλιον ἔλαβον "took counsel" is rendered conspired.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

27:2.sourceText: καὶ δήσαντες αὐτὸν ἀπήγαγον καὶ παρέδωκαν Πειλάτῳ τῷ ἡγεμόνι.
27:2.targetText: They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.

groups.note: The one object αὐτόν serves all three verbs; BSB repeats Him with each.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

27:3.sourceText: Τότε ἰδὼν Ἰούδας ὁ παραδοὺς αὐτὸν ὅτι κατεκρίθη, μεταμεληθεὶς ἔστρεψεν τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ πρεσβυτέροις
27:3.targetText: When Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

groups.note: The participle ἰδών is rendered as a When-clause.
The article with the participle, "the one who handed over", is rendered who had betrayed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τότε (then) untranslated; the participle is rendered as a When-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of κατεκρίθη.
English coordinator; the participle μεταμεληθείς is rendered as a finite verb.

27:4.sourceText: λέγων Ἥμαρτον παραδοὺς αἷμα ἀθῷον. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς; σὺ ὄψῃ.
27:4.targetText: “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood,” he said.  “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.”

groups.note: ὄψῃ "you will see to it" is rendered as the idiom bear the responsibility.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb; the Greek question Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς is verbless.

27:5.sourceText: καὶ ῥίψας τὰ ἀργύρια εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἀνεχώρησεν, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπήγξατο.
27:5.targetText: So Judas threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle ῥίψας.
English coordinator; the participle ῥίψας is rendered as a finite verb, threw.
English coordinator; the participle ἀπελθών is rendered as a finite verb, went away.

27:6.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια εἶπαν Οὐκ ἔξεστιν βαλεῖν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν κορβανᾶν, ἐπεὶ τιμὴ αἵματός ἐστιν.
27:6.targetText: The chief priests picked up the pieces of silver and said, “It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money.”

groups.note: Οὐκ ἔξεστιν "it is not permitted" is rendered It is unlawful.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle λαβόντες is rendered as a finite verb, picked up.

27:7.sourceText: συμβούλιον δὲ λαβόντες ἠγόρασαν ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως εἰς ταφὴν τοῖς ξένοις.
27:7.targetText: After conferring together, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.

groups.note: συμβούλιον λαβόντες "having taken counsel" is rendered After conferring together.
ἐξ "out of" marks the silver as the means of payment, rendered used.
The pronoun αὐτῶν (them, the pieces of silver) is rendered the money.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

27:8.sourceText: διὸ ἐκλήθη ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος Ἀγρὸς αἵματος ἕως τῆς σήμερον.
27:8.targetText: That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

groups.note: ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος "that field" is rendered by the pronoun it.
τῆς σήμερον "the today" is rendered this day.

27:9.sourceText: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἱερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ,
27:9.targetText: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:  “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Him by the people of Israel,

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the thing spoken", is rendered what was spoken.
τοῦ τετιμημένου "of the one priced" names the one on whom the price was set.
ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο "whom they priced" is rendered set, with its agent given as by the people of Israel.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντος (saying) is represented only by the colon before the quotation.
BSB leaves the opening connective καί of the quotation untranslated.

27:10.sourceText: καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως, καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι Κύριος.
27:10.targetText: and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord had commanded me.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

27:11.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ ἡγεμὼν λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη Σὺ λέγεις.
27:11.targetText: Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned Him: “Are You the King of the Jews?”  “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

groups.note: ὁ ἡγεμών "the governor", named again as subject, is rendered by the relative who.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins the clause with the relative who instead of rendering καί.

27:12.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο.
27:12.targetText: And when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He gave no answer.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive marks time: when.

27:13.sourceText: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πειλᾶτος Οὐκ ἀκούεις πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
27:13.targetText: Then Pilate asked Him, “Do You not hear how many charges they are bringing against You?”

groups.note: καταμαρτυροῦσιν "they testify against" is rendered charges they are bringing against.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

27:14.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲ ἓν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.
27:14.targetText: But Jesus gave no answer, not even to a single charge, much to the governor’s amazement.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render αὐτῷ (him) after gave no answer.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἀπεκρίθη.

27:15.sourceText: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν εἰώθει ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀπολύειν ἕνα τῷ ὄχλῳ δέσμιον ὃν ἤθελον.
27:15.targetText: Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing.

groups.note: The pluperfect εἰώθει "was accustomed" is rendered it was … custom.
ὃν ἤθελον "whom they wanted" is rendered of their choosing.

27:16.sourceText: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον Βαραββᾶν.
27:16.targetText: At that time they were holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.

27:17.sourceText: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πειλᾶτος Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν, Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον Χριστόν;
27:17.targetText: So when the crowd had assembled, Pilate asked them, “Which one do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”

groups.note: The genitive absolute συνηγμένων αὐτῶν is rendered as a when-clause.
The pronoun αὐτῶν (they) is rendered the crowd.
The article with the participle, "the one called", is rendered who is called.

27:18.sourceText: ᾔδει γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παρέδωκαν αὐτόν.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a cleft frame to focus out of envy; the Greek has none.

27:19.sourceText: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ λέγουσα Μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ· πολλὰ γὰρ ἔπαθον σήμερον κατ’ ὄναρ δι’ αὐτόν.

groups.note: The genitive absolute Καθημένου αὐτοῦ is rendered as a While-clause.

The participle λέγουσα (saying) is rendered this message.
